sources.heading: Las condiciones de la oración:
sources.text:
Para realizar la oración, se debe cumplir ciertas condiciones que son:

- **La purificación:** incluye la purificación del cuerpo y del lugar de todas las impurezas e incluye también la ablución menor (wudu) y mayor (ghusl).
- **Cubrir la parte íntima (A’ura) que es todo lo que se cubre en presencia de la gente.** En cuanto a la parte íntima del hombre que tiene que cubrir al rezar es entre el ombligo y las rodillas, mientras que la mujer debe tapar todo su cuerpo salvo el rostro y las dos manos.
- **Dirigirse hacia la Quibla que es la dirección hacia la Kaaba honrada que se encuentra en la Meca,** el orante debe dirigirse hacia ella al rezar.
- **La llegada del tiempo del rezo:** no se debe rezar antes del tiempo de la oración, ni se debe retrasarla hasta que pase su tiempo, y lo mejor es realizarla al inicio de su tiempo prescrito.

sources.heading: Introduction
sources.text: In his life, a Muslim performs a number of acts of worship whereby he draws closer to his Creator, Glory is to Him. We do such acts to glorify Allah Almighty and submit to Him alone. The more a Muslim’s heart glorifies Allah, Exalted be He, the greater the effect of doing so is on his worship. A true Muslim dedicates all life, including the time he spends at work, sleeping and having fun, to Allah Almighty, bearing in mind the verse: ⁨﴿قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِى وَنُسُكِى وَمَحْيَاىَ وَمَمَاتِى لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ ۝ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُۥ وَبِذَٰلِكَ أُمِرْتُ وَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾⁩ (Say, "Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allāh, Lord of the worlds. No partner has He. And this I have been commanded, and I am the first [among you] of the Muslims.") (Soorat Al-An’aam, 6:162-163) In this lesson, we are going to learn about the meaning of worship, its types, the conditions that must be met for it to be accepted, and its levels.

sources.heading: The Meaning of Worship
sources.text: By worship is meant everything that Allah has enjoined on us for us to draw closer to Him. It comprises all words and deeds that Allah loves, whether they are outward like the physical acts of worship, such as the prayer and pilgrimage, or inward, like the acts of worship involving the heart, such as love of Allah, fearing His punishment and hoping for His mercy. A person can transform everyday habits into acts of worship simply by having a good intention. If, for instance, he eats, drinks and sleeps with the intention of gaining enough strength to worship Allah better, he will certainly be rewarded for doing so

sources.heading: Types of Acts of Worship
sources.text:
Acts of worship fall into different categories:

| Acts of worship involving the heart | A Muslim performs these with his heart. Examples include love, fear, hope and *khushoo’*. |
| --- | --- |
| Physical acts of worship | A Muslim performs these physically. Examples include the prayer, *zakaat* and pilgrimage. |
| Acts that are abandoned in obedience to Allah | A Muslim draws closer to his Lord by abandoning the acts He has forbidden him, such as drinking alcohol and committing adultery, or by refraining from certain permissible acts at specific times, such as abstaining from food and drink while fasting. |

> *Ar-Rajaa’*(Hope): This refers to rejoicing in Allah’s grace and hoping for His benevolence, while at the same time ensuring proper reliance on Allah by doing good deeds to the best of one’s ability.
> 
> *Al-khushoo’* is a state of utter humility and calmness and deep concentration into which one gets while performing an act of worship, such as the prayer, bringing about outward composure and tranquillity.

sources.heading: Conditions for Acts of Worship to Be Accepted
sources.text:
For an act of worship to be accepted, two conditions must be fulfilled:

The first condition: It has to be done sincerely for the sake of Allah to draw closer to alone, without showing off.

The second condition: It has to be done in the manner Allah has enjoined it and exactly as it was performed by the Prophet ﷺ.

> *Aririyyaa’* (showing off) is the act of doing an act of worship only to be seen and praised by people for doing it.

sources.heading: The Friday Prayer (Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah)
sources.text:
- Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform a special prayer on Friday, called *Salaat-ul-Jumu’ah* (the Friday prayer). It is performed in a special manner, has special conditions and takes the place of the daily *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer on this day.
- Muslims gather together to perform it in the mosque. The *imaam* delivers a two-section *khutbah* (sermon), then he leads them in a two-*rak’ahs* prayer in which he recites the Qur’an aloud.
- It is recommended to take a ritual bath (*ghusl*) to attend the Friday prayer and proceed early to the mosque. It is not permissible to miss it without a legitimate excuse, and if for any reason a person misses it he must perform the four-unit *Dhuhr* (midday) prayer instead but without reciting the Qur’an aloud.
- Women and people on a journey are exempt from performing the Friday prayer.

sources.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
sources.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

Para realizar la oración, se debe cumplir ciertas condiciones que son:

sources.heading: Comment effectuer l’ablution ?
sources.text:
1. Il doit avoir l’intention d’effectuer l’ablution dans son cœur et dire : “Au nom d’Allah.“
2. Il se lave les mains avec de l’eau, en commençant par la [main] droite.
3. Il se lave la bouche en ingurgitant de l’eau, en la gargarisant et ensuite en la recrachant. [En arabe] On appelle cela : “Al Madmadah“
4. Il se lave le nez en aspirant de l’eau et ensuite en l’expirant en faisant ressortir l’air de son nez.
5. Il doit se laver complètement le visage : dans ses limites en longueur, de la racine des cheveux en haut du front jusqu’au bas du menton, ainsi que les poils de la barbe, s’il y en a ; et dans ses limites en largeur, d’une oreille à l’autre.
6. Il se lave les mains, des extrémités des doigts jusqu’à l’articulation du coude, en commençant par la droite.
7. Il mouille ses mains avec de l’eau, puis il s’essuie la tête, en commençant de l’avant de la tête jusqu’à la nuque, puis il revient avec ses mains vers l’avant.
8. Il s’essuie les oreilles avec ses index à l’intérieur des oreilles et il essuie [en même temps] derrière les oreilles avec ses pouces.
9. Il se lave les pieds jusqu’aux chevilles, qui sont les deux os saillants de l’articulation du pied, en commençant par son pied droit.

question: Si on a un rapport avec mon mari mais sans éjaculation, il faut quand même faire le ghusl ?
note: p69: ghusl is required after intercourse whether or not ejaculation takes place.

resp.text: Oui, le lavage rituel (ghusl) est obligatoire après un rapport sexuel, qu’il y ait eu éjaculation ou pas. Le rapport sexuel entre l’homme et la femme entraîne l’état de Janâbah, qui fait partie de l’impureté majeure. Cette impureté majeure nécessite obligatoirement un lavage de l’ensemble du corps avec de l’eau, et la simple ablution ne suffit pas.

sources.heading: Quand le lavage est-il obligatoire ?
sources.text:
Le lavage est obligatoire pour le musulman dans trois cas :

1. L’éjaculation de sperme avec désir, qu’elle ait eu lieu en état d’éveil ou pendant le sommeil.
2. Le rapport sexuel, qu’il y ait eu éjaculation ou pas.
3. La perte du sang des menstrues ou des lochies chez la femme. Et dès lors où le sang ne coule plus, alors la femme doit se laver.

sources.heading: Comment nous lavons-nous ?
sources.text:
Pour se laver, on doit verser de l’eau sur l’ensemble du corps, se rincer la bouche avec de l’eau en se gargarisant, et la recracher, mais aussi aspirer de l’eau par le nez et l’expulser. Si le musulman effectue cela, alors il s’est purifié de l’impureté majeure.

L’impureté majeure désigne ce qu’il est obligatoire d’ôter par le biais du lavage et dont la simple ablution ne suffit pas. Celle-ci est de divers types :
1- L’état de “ Janâbah “ qui résulte suite à un rapport sexuel entre l’homme et la femme, ou l’éjaculation due à un désir même sans rapport sexuel (que ce soit chez l’homme ou la femme).
2- Les menstrues désignent la perte de sang menstruel chez la femme.
3- Les lochies désignent la perte de sang qui survient chez la femme après la sortie du fœtus de son utérus.

sources.heading: Types of Purification
sources.text:
Purification falls into two types:

**Physical Purification**

This means the removal of impurities and the cleansing of the area affected by them

**Moral Purification**

This means the removal of those things that prevent one from performing the prayer, by washing certain parts of the body or the entire body.

Physical purification may be undertaken either by *wudoo’* or *ghusl*

*Wudoo’* (partial ablutions): the ritual washing of certain parts of the body with water

*Ghusl* (full ablutions/bath): the ritual washing of the entire body with water.

Purification must be undertaken with pure water, such as seawater, river water, well water, or any other water that has not been mixed with impurity.

sources.heading: Certain Rulings on Purification
sources.text:
- It is a general Islamic rule that things are naturally clean and pure unless stated otherwise by Islam.
- It would suffice to cleanse the body or clothing of impurities by removing them with water or any cleaning substance that would serve the purpose.
- It would be better for a person who uses the toilet to cleanse the place of urine and faeces with water. It is also permissible for him to cleanse himself with tissues or any other material that serves to remove impurity.

sources.heading: The Manner of Performing *Wudoo’*
sources.text:
1. He intends in his heart to perform *wudoo’* and says, *bismillaah* “In the name of Allah”.
2. He washes his hands up to the wrists with water.
3. He rinses out his mouth thoroughly by moving water around in the mouth and then spitting it out. This process is called *madmadah*) in Arabic.
4. He cleans his nose by sniffing water into the nostrils and ejecting it out by blowing his nose.
5. He washes his face thoroughly from the hairline at the top of the forehead to the bottom of the chin, along with the beard, if he is bearded, and from ear to ear.
6. He washes his hands from the fingertips up to the elbow, starting with his right hand.
7. With wet hands, and starting with his hands flat on the top of the head near the hairline, he wipes it to the back of the neck and back to the front.

sources.heading: Los pilares de la fe:
sources.text:
1. **La creencia en Al-láh:** el musulmán cree en la existencia de Al-láh -Enaltecido sea- y en Sus atributos, como Señor de este universo, es el Creador, el Soberano, y Quien maneja todos los asuntos según Su Voluntad, es Él Quien sostiene a sus siervos. Y cree también que Al-láh es el Único que merece ser adorado y el Único que posee los atributos de perfección.
2. **La creencia en los ángeles:** el musulmán cree en la existencia de los nobles ángeles, y que fueron creados por Al-láh, que adoran a Al-láh y nunca Le desobedecen. Cree también en sus características y en sus roles como fueron mencionados en el Corán y en la sunnah profética.
3. **La creencia en los Libros revelados:** el musulmán cree que Al-láh ha revelado libros a Sus siervos a través de los mensajeros, estos libros fueron revelados para guiar a la gente y enseñarla los asuntos religiosos. Entre estos libros se encuentra la Torá revelada al profeta Moisés ibn Imrán -la paz sea con él-, los Salmos revelados a David -la paz sea con él-, el Evangelio a Jesús hijo de María -la paz sea con ambos- y el Corán a Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- y fue el último y el dominante.
4. **La creencia en los profetas -la paz sea con ellos-:** el musulmán cree que Al-láh ha enviado mensajeros para sus pueblos y les apoyaba con milagros que indican su veracidad, para transmitir la buena noticia a los creyentes y para advertir a los incrédulos, para enseñar a sus pueblos los asuntos religiosos. Sin embargo cada pueblo debe creer en el mensajero enviado a él obedeciéndole y siguiéndole y que Muhammad -que la paz y las bendiciones de Al-láh sean con él- es el último de los mensajeros enviados.
5. **La creencia en el Día de Juicio:** el musulmán cree en el día de Resurrección, y cree que Al-láh resucita a los muertos de sus tumbas y serán juzgados y recompensados por sus actos, unos entrarán al paraíso y otros al fuego de infierno.

sources.text:

This includes meat served in restaurants and shops in countries where Muslims or People of the Book constitute a minority.
2. The meat of animals killed by a Muslim or a member of the People of the Book is lawful based on textual evidence to this effect in the Qur’an.
3. The meat of animals that are not killed according to Islamic law, such as by electrocution and drowning, is strictly forbidden.
4. The general rule is that it is permissible to consume the flesh of animals slaughtered by People of the Book as well as meat of animals generally found in their restaurants and shops, making sure, however, to invoke Allah’s name at the time of eating (that is, by saying *Bismillaah*), but it is better for Muslims to eat only meat that has been proven to be lawful (*halaal*).

sources.heading: What Are the Conditions for Islamic Slaughter?
sources.text:
Islamic slaughter is one that satisfies the following conditions:

1. The person undertaking the slaughtering process must be Muslim, Jew or Christian who has reached the age of discretion and carries out this act for the intended purpose.
2. The tool used for slaughter must be suitable for the intended purpose, causes blood to flow and sharp, such as a knife. It is forbidden to use anything that may kill the animal due to its heavy weight, hit its head to death or render it unconscious by resorting to electric stunning, for instance.
3. The name of Allah must be pronounced by saying *Bismillaah* (in the name of Allah) at the time of slaughtering the animal.
4. Cutting what must be cut in the Islamic slaughter, namely, the oesophagus, the throat, and the two jugular veins, or just three of these four.

sources.text: Имущественные отношения — это деловые отношения между людьми, в процессе которых происходит обмен имущества, будь это обмен одного имущество на другое, как купля-продажа; или обмен имущества на удовлетворение какой-либо потребности, как аренда; или передача имущества без получения чего-либо взамен, как подарки.

sources.heading: Основа в имущественных отношениях
sources.text:
Основной в имущественных отношениях является дозволенность. Запрещены лишь те из них, запрет на которые пришел в Коране или Сунне..

> Основой в мирских делах, к которым относятся и имущественные отношения, является дозволенность, поэтому запрет в этой области возможен лишь на основе доказательств. Это коренное отличие мирской сферы от обрядов поклонения, основа которых полностью противоположна: не дозволено совершать ни один из видов поклонения, если ни в Коране, ни в Сунне нет доказательств дозволенности его совершения.

sources.heading: Запрещенные виды имущественных отношений
sources.text:
Всевышний Аллах запретил некоторые виды имущественных отношений:

- Присвоение чужого имущества без права, например, обманом или силой.
- Принуждение одного из участников к сделке, которую он не хочет заключать.
- Торговля товарами, вредными для здоровья человека, такими как алкоголь, наркотики, табак и другие.
- Ростовщичество, то есть ссуда денег при условии их возврата с добавлением некоторого процента от заемных денег, например, ты должен отдать на 5% больше денег, чем занимал.
- Продажа неизвестного товара, например, ящика, содержимое которого неизвестно.
- Азартные игры и пари, в которых победитель забирает деньги проигравшего.

sources.heading: Introduction
sources.text: Islam urges its followers to observe high moral character. The Prophet ﷺ stressed the importance of morals in many of his traditions, combining many acts of worship Muslims perform with good moral character. Islam promises a Muslim who displays such good character great rewards both in this world and the hereafter. In this lesson, we are going to learn about the importance of good moral character in Islam, as well as some of its virtues.

sources.heading: Good Moral Character in Islam
sources.text:
- Good moral character occupies a lofty position in Islam, as it is one of the important objectives of *Sharee‘ah* and one of the goals behind the Prophet’s mission.
- Good moral character is closely linked to faith, and the believers with complete faith are those who demonstrate the best moral character.
- A Muslim will be rewarded for his good manners, just as he will be rewarded for the prayer and fasting.

sources.heading: Some Virtues of Good Moral Character
sources.text:
- The Prophet ﷺ informs us that the act that will cause people to enter Paradise the most will be piety and good character.
- He ﷺ states that the heaviest of a person’s good deeds that will be placed on the scales of deeds on the Day of Resurrection will be good moral character.
- He ﷺ further states that the closest believers to him on the Day of Resurrection will be those who possess good moral character.

> **The scales of deeds:** This will be on the Day of Resurrection when a person’s good and bad deeds will be weighed in a balance, whose shape or size none knows but Allah. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be admitted into Paradise, but those whose bad deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be sent to Hell.

sources.heading: Domains of Good Moral Character in Islam:
sources.text:
Good moral character in Islam is not restricted to one domain; rather, it covers many of them, namely:

- Good moral character vis-à-vis Allah Almighty, such as by devoting oneself sincerely to Him and showing total obedience to Him.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis the Prophet ﷺ, such as by loving him, respecting him, showing politeness when talking about him and invoking Allah’s peace and blessings upon him when his name is mentioned.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis Allah’s laws, such as by honouring and obeying them.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis oneself, such as by gently encouraging oneself to show obedience to Allah and firmly avoiding laziness in this respect.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis others, such as by being honest and trustworthy.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis animals, such as by showing kindness to them and not being cruel to them.
- Good moral character vis-à-vis the environment, such as by preserving it, planting trees and not being extravagant with its natural resources.

sources.heading: The Five Obligatory Prayers
sources.text:
Allah Almighty has enjoined Muslims to perform five prayers throughout the day and night, namely:

| The Prayer | Beginning Time | Ending Time | Number of units (*rak‘ahs*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Fajr* (Dawn) Prayer | at the break of dawn | sunrise | 2 |
| *Dhuhr* (Midday) Prayer | when the sun starts declining westward at midday after reaching its zenith | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | 4 |
| *‘Asr* (Late Afternoon) Prayer | when the shadow of an object becomes equal in length to the object itself | sunset | 4 |
| *Maghrib* (Sunset) Prayer | sunset | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | 3 |
| *‘Ishaa’* (Late Evening) Prayer | when the red glow (evening twilight) on the western horizon disappears | midnight | 4 |

sources.heading: The Conditions of the Prayer
sources.text:
- Purity: Once’s body and the place where the prayer is to be performed must be cleansed from physical impurities, and any ritual impurity must be removed with *wudoo’* or *ghusl*.
- Covering the intimate parts of the body (*‘awrah*): The word *‘awrah* refers to the parts of the body that must be covered in front of people. A man’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer extends from the navel to the knees; a woman’s *‘awrah* that must be covered during the prayer is her entire body except for the face and hands.
- Facing the *qiblah*: The *qiblah* is the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah. One must, therefore, pray in the direction of the Ka‘bah in Makkah.
- When its appointed time becomes due: The prayer will not be valid if it is performed before its time has started. It is not permissible to delay it beyond its due time, and it is best to perform it at the beginning of its time.

sources.heading: The General Islamic Rule Regarding Financial Transactions in Islam
sources.text:
The general Islamic rule is that all types of transactions are permissible, and that none of them is forbidden unless declared as such in the Qur’an or the Prophet’s *Sunnah*.

> The general Islamic rule regarding transactions in general, including financial transactions, is that they are permissible, and thus nothing is considered impermissible without evidence, as opposed to acts of worship, where the general rule regarding them is that they are not permissible unless there is evidence which states otherwise.

sources.heading: Prohibited Forms of Financial Transactions
sources.text:
**Allah Almighty has forbidden some financial transactions, including the following:**

- The unlawful taking of other people’s property, such as by using deceptive tricks or by force.
- Conducting a transaction under coercion, such as by forcing someone to enter into a transaction against his will.
- Trafficking in substances that are injurious to human health, such as alcohol, drugs and tobacco.
- Charging interest on loans, an example of which is to lend money to someone on condition that the borrower must pay, say, 5% on the borrowed amount to the lender.
- Selling things that are not known, such as selling a box the contents of which are unknown.
- Gambling and betting whereby the winner unlawfully takes the money of the loser.

sources.heading: Основа в имущественных отношениях
sources.text:
Основной в имущественных отношениях является дозволенность. Запрещены лишь те из них, запрет на которые пришел в Коране или Сунне..

> Основой в мирских делах, к которым относятся и имущественные отношения, является дозволенность, поэтому запрет в этой области возможен лишь на основе доказательств. Это коренное отличие мирской сферы от обрядов поклонения, основа которых полностью противоположна: не дозволено совершать ни один из видов поклонения, если ни в Коране, ни в Сунне нет доказательств дозволенности его совершения.

sources.heading: Условия принятия поклонения
sources.text:
Для того чтобы поклонение было принято, необходимо соблюдение двух условий. Первое — искренность перед Аллахом: совершение поклонения с целью приблизиться к Одному лишь Аллаху, без придания Ему сотоварищей в этом и без показухи.

> Показуха (рия’) — совершение мусульманином поклонения для того, чтобы люди увидели, как он его совершает, и похвалили его за это.

Второе — соответствие Шариату Аллаха: совершение поклонения так, как было предписано Всевышним Аллахом, и так, как совершал его Пророк ﷺ.
